## Intent
Hypothesis: LP1 unrolling by 4 exposes component-wise vectorization on identity-ordered AoS that can approach the streaming ceiling despite branchy respawn.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (10000–10000000) exceed the L2 spill at N≈7710, so every point already resides in L3 or DRAM. At death_q=0.01, ns/p stays nearly flat: 25.43 at N=10000 (L3-resident, 680 KB), 25.563 at N=100000 (still L3, 6.8 MB), 26.967 at N=1000000 (past the L3 spill at N≈246723, 68 MB in DRAM), and 26.207 at N=10000000. The L3→DRAM transition produces only a ~5.5% rise (25.563→26.967), not a knee. Death rate raises the floor uniformly — q=0.5 lifts ns/p to ~34 at every N — without altering the flat N-shape. The absence of any cache-spill knee confirms the algo is not bandwidth-limited; cost is dominated by per-particle overhead insensitive to working-set residency.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.67 GB/s at N=10000, death_q=0.01 — 21% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth is essentially constant across N (2.52–2.67 GB/s at q=0.01), confirming the algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Death rate monotonically reduces effective bandwidth: 2.67→2.54→2.33→1.99 GB/s as q goes 0.01→0.1→0.25→0.5, reflecting rising branchy-respawn cost. There is no regime where the algo approaches the ceiling; it never enters a bandwidth-bound regime. The 67–69% frontend-stall share (with 0.0% backend stalls) at every measured point identifies instruction fetch/decode as the bottleneck, not data movement.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within each particle, not across particles. The LP1-unroll loop processes 4 particles per iteration (stride 0x110 = 272 = 4×68 bytes), using `vmovups` for 16-byte loads, `vmovsd` for 8-byte loads, `vbroadcastss` for scalar constants, and `vmulps`/`vaddps` for packed 4×float arithmetic; `vinsertps` and `vshufps` shuffle components within registers. There is no gather — all loads are base+offset (`rbx+r15*1+disp`), contiguous per particle, and vector-suffixed instructions total 0. The render loop (LP2-simple) performs byte-granular scatter stores: `mov BYTE PTR [rcx+r11*1], r12b` with `cmovae` saturation to 0xff. The 791-instruction footprint with 40 `cmp`, 23 `vucomiss`, and 17 `jmp` explains the 67–69% frontend stalls — the decoder cannot keep up with the branchy control flow and RNG logic, starving execution units regardless of the component-wise SIMD.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 2.67 GB/s (21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate, and the flat ns/p curve (25.43→26.207 at q=0.01 across N=10000–10000000) shows it is frontend-stall-bound (67.7%), not bandwidth-bound. Component-wise vectorization (`vmulps`/`vaddps` on per-particle components) cannot compensate for the 791-instruction branchy footprint, and the byte-granular render scatter further prevents streaming. LP1 unrolling does not approach the streaming ceiling.
